name: Fruit press
description: A heavy wooden press with an iron screw over a slatted basket. Squeezes juice and oil out of fruit, seeds and mash.
notes: Drawn as a placed cider press 500 by 440 mm and 900 mm tall, oak with iron-dull screw, hoops and tommy bar, and dark gaps between the basket staves. pressing 1 sits below the hydraulic press's 2. The size is a placeholder for a thing too heavy to carry. The box is large because the frame stands round open space.

name: Woven sieve
description: A shallow round tray woven from plant strips. The weave is tight enough to sift flour from bran.
notes: Crafted, so it has no loot economy. 240 mm across and 45 mm deep: straw-wicker tray and coiled plant-dried rim over a two-tone basket weave on a dark bark floor that shows the openings. The box counts the open tray.

name: Test sieve
description: A round stainless laboratory sieve with a fine woven mesh. Grades powders and grain, and sifts flour very fine.
notes: 200 mm across and 50 mm tall with a stepped skirt for stacking and a brass label plate on the front. The mesh is a 4 mm grid of steel-bright wires over a steel-grey disc, since no fine steel mesh finish exists. Medical stands for the laboratories that use these. The box counts the open frame.

name: Wire sieve
description: A disc of fine steel mesh caught in a loop of stiff wire, the wire ends twisted into a handle.
notes: Crafted, so it has no loot economy. A 130 mm loop with a 120 mm twisted handle ending in a hanging loop, 276 mm overall, lying flat; held by the handle. Mesh drawn as stainless strands over a steel-grey disc.

name: Shaved ice maker
description: A countertop machine that shaves ice into fluffy snow for snow cones. Needs power.
notes: 240 by 200 mm and 300 mm tall: red housing, clear hopper with ice under a white push lid, white chute and a clear catch tray holding shaved ice. The tiles draw plastic-clear opaque. Making shaved ice is a recipe matter for the refactor, and its power draw has no content field yet.

name: Copper still
description: A copper pot still: a boiler with a domed head, a swan-neck arm and a water-cooled coil tub with a tap. Makes spirits and other distillates over a fire.
notes: A boiler 300 mm across under a column and helmet with a thermometer dial, the arm stepping down to a steel-galvanised worm tub of water, 628 by 560 mm overall. distilling is a new quality name. Capacity 8 L is a judgement from the boiler. The box counts the arm and tub beside it. The small closed loop extractor rides here, though a steel solvent extractor would read better on its own model.

name: Home-made mess kit
description: A kerosene burner, a lidded billy can and a jar of fuel, put together by hand to cook anywhere.
notes: Crafted, so it has no loot economy. Laid out together, 244 mm across: a stainless billy 140 mm across with a lifted wire bail, a burner with a brass head, pump and three pot supports, a stoppered glass jar of fuel-amber kerosene and a spoon. heating is the quality name used for hotplates; the burner's fuel has no content field yet.

name: Teapot
description: A small stainless teapot with a lid, a spout and a loop handle.
notes: 120 mm across and 124 mm tall, 186 mm from the spout tip to the black grip. Capacity 1 L is a judgement from the body.

name: Toaster
description: A two-slice electric toaster with a carriage lever and a browning dial. Needs power.
notes: 270 by 160 mm and 190 mm tall: brushed steel shell on a black base, two slots painted flush, and the lever, dial and red cancel button on a black strip at the front right. steel-stainless stands for the aluminium shell. Toasting is a recipe matter, and its power draw has no content field yet.

name: Vacuum sealer
description: A countertop heat sealer with an air pump. Draws the air out of a plastic bag and seals it shut, so food keeps far longer. Needs power.
notes: 350 by 150 mm and 88 mm tall: a steel-stainless base under a black lid with grey latches at each end, a button strip along the front and a bag cutter rail with a red slider. vacuum_sealing is a new quality name for its use on bagged food.

name: Waffle iron
description: A hinged pair of round aluminium moulds on long handles. Bakes waffles over a stove or a fire.
notes: A stovetop iron 302 mm long: a closed mould 160 mm across with a cast grid on top, a hinge block at the back and two arms with wood-walnut grips, as most irons have.

name: Sand water filter
description: A bucket packed with sand over gravel, with a tap low on the side. Water poured in comes out clearer and mostly safe, but not always.
notes: Crafted, so it has no loot economy. A white 20 litre pail 300 mm across and 370 mm tall, brick-buff sand with a ring of stone-grey gravel round the inlet, the bail folded back and a blue drip tap at the front. No sand finish exists; brick-buff is closest. Very heavy, so it is drafted as a workstation; water_purification 1 is the hand-held level the stationary purifier's notes left room for, and how often it fails is a rule for the refactor.

name: Portable water purifier
description: A battery-powered purifier with a pump, a filter canister and an intake hose. Makes water from a stream safe to drink.
notes: A grey housing 110 by 90 mm and 215 mm tall with a green display, buttons and battery door on the front, a clear blue canister with a white cartridge on its side, an outlet spout on top and a frosted intake hose coiled behind. water_purification 1 is the level the stationary purifier's notes left for a hand-held one. Battery use has no content field yet. The box is large because it counts the coiled hose.
